# **1\. Product structure**

I would structure the app around **9 core modules**.

| Module | Purpose |
| ----- | ----- |
| 🏠 **Today / Dashboard** | What matters right now |
| ✅ **Tasks & Calendar** | Tasks, events, schedules |
| 🔥 **Habits** | Repeating habits, streaks, consistency |
| 🌅 **Routine** | Morning/day/night routines from your supplied file |
| 🗺️ **Roadmap** | Long-term goals and milestones from your file |
| 🎯 **Focus** | Forest-style focus timer \+ sessions |
| 💰 **Expenses** | Spending, budgets, categories |
| 📊 **Overview** | Long-term statistics and progress |
| ⚙️ **Settings** | Account, notifications, themes, gamification |

The navigation could look roughly like:

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐

│ LIFEQUEST                                           │

│                                                     │

│ 🏠 Today                                            │

│ 📊 Overview                                         │

│                                                     │

│ ✅ Tasks                                            │

│ 📅 Calendar                                         │

│ 🔥 Habits                                           │

│ 🌅 Routine                                          │

│ 🗺️ Roadmap                                          │

│ 🎯 Focus                                            │

│ 💰 Expenses                                         │

│                                                     │

│ ─────────────────────────────────────────────────── │

│                                                     │

│ Level 12                                           │

│ ████████████░░  78%                                │

│ 2,840 XP                                            │

│ 🔥 14 day streak                                    │

└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

On mobile, this becomes a bottom navigation with a **More** menu.

# **2\. The most important design decision: the game system**

Don't make gamification a decorative layer.

Make it part of the underlying application logic.

For example:

### **Completing a task**

Complete task

      ↓

Determine task difficulty

      ↓

Award XP

      ↓

Update daily progress

      ↓

Update streak

      ↓

Check achievements

      ↓

Update roadmap progress

      ↓

Update level

      ↓

Trigger visual reward

Example:

Complete "Study React — 60 min"

\+25 XP

\+1 Focus session

\+1 Daily task

\+5% Daily progress

\+1 Roadmap milestone progress

🔥 Streak maintained

This is what will make the application feel **alive**.

---

# **3\. Gamification system**

I would use **light RPG mechanics**, rather than turning the entire app into a cartoon game.

### **Player**

Level

XP

Current streak

Longest streak

Daily score

Weekly score

Monthly score

Total completed tasks

Focus hours

Habit consistency

Roadmap completion

### **XP**

Start with something simple:

| Activity | Base XP |
| ----- | ----- |
| Small task | \+5 |
| Normal task | \+10 |
| Difficult task | \+20 |
| Major milestone | \+50 |
| Habit completion | \+5 |
| Routine completion | \+10 |
| Focus session | \+10 per 25 min |
| Major roadmap milestone | \+100 |

Don't make XP mathematically complicated in v1.

### **Levels**

Something like:

Level 1 → 0 XP

Level 2 → 100 XP

Level 3 → 250 XP

Level 4 → 450 XP

Level 5 → 700 XP

...

Later you can tune the curve based on real usage.

### **Rewards**

Use:

* XP animations  
* streak flames  
* achievement badges  
* level-up animations  
* completion particles  
* progress bars  
* unlockable themes  
* avatar/frame customization  
* milestone celebrations

Avoid things such as:

> "You failed today."

Instead:

> "Reset complete. Let's get back on track."

The app should encourage **recovery**, not punish missed days.

# **11\. Recommended technology stack**

I'd deliberately keep this stack relatively simple.

### **Frontend**

**Next.js \+ TypeScript**

Next.js is currently positioned as a full-stack React framework, so you don't need a separate frontend/backend project for this application. ([Next.js](https://nextjs.org/docs?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

### **UI**

**Tailwind CSS \+ shadcn/ui \+ Base UI**

shadcn/ui is particularly appropriate for an AI-built project because its components are actual source code inside your project rather than a closed abstraction. That makes it easier for Claude to modify consistently. Current shadcn projects use Base UI as the default primitive layer. ([shadcn/ui](https://ui.shadcn.com/docs?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

### **Animations**

**Motion for React**

Use it for:

* progress animation  
* XP gain  
* level-up  
* card transitions  
* completion effects  
* page transitions  
* focus timer animations

Motion for React is designed for production React animations and supports spring/layout/gesture animations. ([Motion](https://motion.dev/docs/react?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

### **Backend / database**

**Supabase**

Use:

PostgreSQL

Supabase Auth

Supabase Storage

Supabase Realtime

Supabase Edge Functions

Supabase provides PostgreSQL directly and integrates Auth, Storage, Realtime and Edge Functions around that database. ([Supabase](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/database/overview?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

Its current Next.js setup supports cookie-based authentication and TypeScript/Tailwind scaffolding. ([Supabase](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/auth/quickstarts/nextjs?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

### **Validation**

**Zod**

For:

* task forms  
* expense forms  
* routine configuration  
* settings  
* API/server-action validation

### **Forms**

**React Hook Form**

### **Dates**

**date-fns**

### **Charts**

**Recharts**

### **State**

I'd use:

Server/data state → Next.js \+ Supabase

Client UI state    → Zustand

Form state         → React Hook Form

Don't put your entire application into Zustand.

### **Offline capability**

Later:

**Dexie \+ IndexedDB**

Dexie provides a TypeScript-friendly IndexedDB layer and is appropriate if you add serious offline-first behavior. ([Dexie](https://dexie.org/docs/Typescript?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

---

# **12\. Notifications**

This deserves its own architecture.

Use:

Supabase

   ↓

Scheduled notification job

   ↓

Push service

   ↓

Service Worker

   ↓

Browser / device notification

The Web Push API allows a server to push messages even when the web app isn't currently loaded, while persistent notifications can be displayed through a service worker. ([MDN Web Docs](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Push_API?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

So don't build reminders using only:

setTimeout(...)

That will not be a reliable production notification system.

# **14\. Database architecture**

A reasonable starting schema:

profiles

categories

tasks

task\_occurrences

task\_completions

habits

habit\_completions

routines

routine\_items

routine\_completions

goals

goal\_milestones

roadmap\_nodes

calendar\_events

focus\_sessions

expenses

expense\_categories

budgets

reminders

notification\_preferences

xp\_events

achievements

user\_achievements

user\_stats

Important principle:

### **Don't store only the current score.**

Store the **events** that generated the score.

For example:

xp\_events

id

user\_id

source\_type

source\_id

xp\_amount

created\_at

Then you can reconstruct:

Total XP

Daily XP

Weekly XP

Monthly XP

XP from habits

XP from tasks

XP from focus

This will make analytics and debugging much easier.

# **16\. Design direction**

I would **not** make it cartoonish.

The visual target should be:

> **Premium dark productivity system \+ subtle RPG \+ modern dashboard**

Think:

* dark graphite background  
* glass/soft-surface cards  
* vivid accent colors  
* subtle gradients  
* glowing progress indicators  
* smooth microanimations  
* large visual statistics  
* compact typography  
* rounded but not excessively bubbly  
* satisfying completion interactions

The interface should feel like:

**"This is my command center."**

Not:

**"This is a children's game."**

Some visual directions that are useful as references:

![Image][image2]

![Image][image3]

![Image][image4]

These are references for the visual language only; don't copy their layouts or branding.

# **18\. How I would build it in Claude**

This is where many AI-coded projects go wrong.

**Do not give Claude one gigantic prompt saying "build the whole app."**

It will generate a huge amount of code, make inconsistent decisions, and eventually lose track of architecture.

Instead, use **phases**.

---

# **Phase 0 — Give Claude the project constitution**

This is the first prompt.

You are the lead software architect and senior full-stack engineer for this project.

We are building a production-quality gamified personal Life OS called "LifeQuest".

You must prioritize:

\- maintainability

\- type safety

\- clean architecture

\- reusable components

\- responsive design

\- accessibility

\- security

\- simple deployment

\- database integrity

\- excellent UX

TECH STACK

Frontend:

\- Next.js App Router

\- TypeScript

\- Tailwind CSS

\- shadcn/ui

\- Base UI

\- Motion for React

Backend:

\- Supabase

\- PostgreSQL

\- Supabase Auth

\- Supabase Edge Functions where necessary

Libraries:

\- Zod

\- React Hook Form

\- date-fns

\- Recharts

\- Zustand where client-side global state is actually required

Use modern stable versions available at project creation.

PROJECT PRINCIPLES

1\. Do not over-engineer.

2\. Avoid duplicate business logic.

3\. Database logic must be centralized.

4\. Server-side authorization must never depend solely on client-side checks.

5\. Users must only be able to access their own data.

6\. Use Supabase Row Level Security.

7\. Keep UI components reusable.

8\. Separate business logic from presentation.

9\. Avoid huge components.

10\. Prefer composition.

11\. Use TypeScript strictly.

12\. Validate external/user input.

13\. Make mobile support first-class.

14\. Keep animations subtle and purposeful.

15\. Respect reduced-motion accessibility settings.

GAMIFICATION

The application has:

\- XP

\- levels

\- streaks

\- achievements

\- milestones

All XP changes must be represented as events.

CORE FEATURES

\- dashboard

\- tasks

\- calendar

\- habits

\- routines

\- roadmap

\- focus timer

\- expenses

\- reminders

\- analytics

\- notifications

FILES

The project must contain:

/docs/PRODUCT\_SPEC.md

/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md

/docs/DATABASE.md

/docs/DESIGN\_SYSTEM.md

/docs/STATUS.md

Before implementing major functionality, update these documents when architectural decisions change.

IMPORTANT DEVELOPMENT RULE

Never rewrite unrelated working code simply because you prefer another implementation.

Before modifying a subsystem:

1\. inspect the existing implementation

2\. understand dependencies

3\. make the smallest coherent change

4\. test the change

5\. document the result

At the end of every phase:

\- run type checking

\- run lint

\- run tests

\- fix issues

\- update docs/STATUS.md

Do not proceed into later features until the current phase is stable.

First task:

Create the complete project specification and architecture documents.

Do NOT build the full application yet.

This establishes Claude as an architect rather than an uncontrolled code generator.

# **Phase 2 — Authentication \+ Supabase**

Read all project documentation before modifying the code.

Implement authentication and Supabase infrastructure.

Requirements:

\- Supabase project integration

\- environment variable handling

\- server Supabase client

\- browser Supabase client

\- authentication

\- sign up

\- sign in

\- sign out

\- protected routes

\- profile creation

\- authenticated user context

Use secure cookie-based server-side authentication.

Create the required database migration.

Create Row Level Security policies so that users can only access their own personal data.

Do not create feature tables yet unless required for the user profile.

Test:

\- unauthenticated user cannot access protected pages

\- authenticated user can access own profile

\- user cannot access another user's profile/data

Update:

\- DATABASE.md

\- ARCHITECTURE.md

\- STATUS.md

Supabase's current Next.js guidance specifically supports cookie-based SSR auth through its Next.js integration. ([Supabase](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/auth/quickstarts/nextjs?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

# **Phase 10 — Notifications**

Implement the notification infrastructure.

Requirements:

\- reminder creation

\- reminder editing

\- reminder deletion

\- notification preferences

\- task reminders

\- habit reminders

\- routine reminders

\- roadmap deadline reminders

Support:

\- in-app notifications

\- browser push notifications where supported

Use a service worker and Push API for persistent notifications.

Do not assume notification permission is granted.

Handle:

\- permission denied

\- unsupported browser

\- revoked permission

\- subscription expiration

\- duplicate subscriptions

Never expose private push credentials to the browser.

Create a server-side notification workflow.

Add notification logs for debugging.

Push notifications require an active service worker, and persistent notifications are the appropriate model for mobile web use. ([MDN Web Docs](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Push_API?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

# **22\. One architectural decision I'd make now**

Don't build this as:

Tasks

Habits

Roadmap

Focus

Expenses

as isolated features.

Build it around a common concept:

## **Life Activity**

Activity

├── Task

├── Habit

├── Routine item

├── Focus session

├── Roadmap milestone

└── Event

Then the gamification engine can consume activity events:

Activity completed

       ↓

Completion Event

       ↓

XP

       ↓

Statistics

       ↓

Streak

       ↓

Achievement

       ↓

Goal/Roadmap progress

That architecture will make the application much easier to extend.

---

So the final product architecture becomes:

                        LIFEQUEST

                            │

              ┌─────────────┴─────────────┐

              │                           │

          DAILY LIFE                 LONG-TERM LIFE

              │                           │

      ┌───────┼───────┐             ┌────┴────┐

      │       │       │             │         │

    Tasks   Habits  Routine       Goals     Roadmap

      │       │       │             │         │

      └───────┼───────┘             └────┬────┘

              │                           │

              └─────────────┬─────────────┘

                            │

                       COMPLETION

                            │

                     ┌──────┴──────┐

                     │             │

                    XP          Statistics

                     │             │

                     ↓             ↓

                  LEVELS        OVERVIEW

And around that:

Calendar ←→ Activities

That gives you a coherent **Life OS**, rather than a standard productivity app with a few gamification decorations. 🎮
